title: Pitching and hitting decision register
source_policy: Source IDs resolve in docs/research-pitching-hitting.md. Primary documentation, inherited reports, observations and authored proposals remain distinct.

brief.author: Jack
brief.scope: Research both Mario baseball games and other baseball games, then prepare a tracker for choices we make together.
brief.direction: Loves Mario Super Sluggers and is open to greater robustness; no specific new mechanic or numerical target accepted.

decisions.question: What should added depth primarily ask the player to do?

options.label: Mario-style tactical depth
options.tradeoff: Preserve positioning and charge; deepen pitch mixing, reads and situational choices.

options.label: More precise execution
options.tradeoff: Add target/reticle or release demands; more control, more practice required.

options.label: Clarity and reliability first
options.tradeoff: Keep the current choice set and improve consistency, teaching and feedback before expansion.

decisions.recommendation: A, with clarity and reliability required throughout. It best matches the stated affection for Sluggers; still only a proposal.
decisions.existing_contract: Existing gameplay-spec principles remain; this choice authorizes a direction, not new controls or coefficients.
decisions.acceptance: A new player can put balls in play; a practiced player can explain a tactical advantage beyond simply reacting faster.
decisions.accepted_scope: Pursue Mario-style tactical depth together with reliability, consistency and clear teaching. Exact sequencing remains open. This does not select more demanding aiming/release controls, a specific mechanic, or numerical tuning.

decision_evidence.question: PH-01: tactical depth / execution depth / reliability first

history.author: Jack
history.scope: Pursue Mario-style tactical depth together with reliability, consistency and clear teaching. Exact sequencing remains open. This does not select more demanding aiming/release controls, a specific mechanic, or numerical tuning.

decisions.question: How many ordinary pitch families should each pitcher have?

options.label: Current compact vocabulary
options.tradeoff: Normal, charged and changeup with steering; lowest teaching cost.

options.label: Small authored repertoire
options.tradeoff: Add clearly distinct ordinary pitch shapes, with character-specific strengths and weaknesses.

options.label: Broad baseball repertoire
options.tradeoff: Many named pitches and detailed matchup selection; largest complexity and balance cost.

decisions.recommendation: B if PH-01 favors added tactics; define each pitch by a distinct response it demands before choosing a count or names.
decisions.existing_contract: Current PitchFlight has fastball/changeup base shapes; stars are separate. No new pitch count is selected.
decisions.acceptance: Each pitch has a readable trajectory, tactical use, counterplay and reason not to throw it every time.
decisions.accepted_scope: Develop distinct ordinary pitches with clear tactical purposes, readable behavior and weaknesses. PH-02-R1 fixes exactly three ordinary pitches per pitcher, with character-specific selections from a shared library; charging modifies a pitch and Star Pitches sit outside the count. PH-02-R2 fixes the library as fastball, changeup, curveball, slider and sinker with their recorded game roles. Character assignments, universal access, detailed weaknesses/counterplay, selection inputs and numerical tuning remain open; location and steering follow PH-03/PH-04. This is direction acceptance, not implementation or human playtest acceptance. Original scopes are preserved in history and each refinement.

ordinary_pitch_library.role: A faster dipping alternative to the curveball.

decision_evidence.question: PH-02-R2: What should the shared pitch library contain? Proposed game roles: Fastball: speed pressure, relatively straight; Changeup: slower delivery that punishes early swings; Curveball: pronounced arc and drop; Slider: sideways movement that challenges coverage; Sinker: a faster dipping alternative to the curveball. Each character gets three from that library. 1. All five (recommended): more distinct character combinations. 2. Four, leaving out the sinker: fewer shapes to learn and less overlap between dropping pitches.

decisions.question: How does the pitcher choose location?

options.label: Mound and shape
options.tradeoff: Keep horizontal mound positioning and pitch-defined height.

options.label: Coarse zone intent
options.tradeoff: Choose a broad region before delivery; execution and shape determine the actual crossing.

options.label: Free two-dimensional target
options.tradeoff: Place an exact intended endpoint; increases precision and aiming load.

decisions.recommendation: Compare A and B first. Choose together with PH-04 so aiming plus steering does not grant unlimited correction.
decisions.existing_contract: Human pitching currently has no free vertical aim. CPU endpoint targeting is a baseline asymmetry to assess in PH-18.
decisions.acceptance: Both seats can intentionally seek a strike or chase pitch without the shared screen revealing the exact endpoint.
decisions.accepted_scope: Use horizontal mound positioning plus pitch-defined height to choose location. Do not add broad target-region selection or a freely aimed two-dimensional target under this decision. Exact pitch shapes and numerical values remain open; post-release steering is the separate PH-04 decision. Direction acceptance only, with no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-03: 1. Mound position + pitch shape; 2. Choose a broad target area; 3. Aim freely within a two-dimensional target. Post-release steering follows separately.

decisions.question: How much control remains after release?

options.label: Live lateral steering
options.tradeoff: Keep the familiar post-release duel; requires bounded break and a fair response opportunity.

options.label: Committed shape
options.tradeoff: Release locks the path; easier prediction and clearer pitch identity.

options.label: Bounded early steering
options.tradeoff: Allow a limited correction then commit; adds a timing boundary to teach.

decisions.recommendation: A as the first comparison baseline; evaluate B/C only against an observed readability or fairness problem.
decisions.existing_contract: Current break is accumulated direction input, with charge/changeup damping. New caps and cutoffs remain unset.
decisions.acceptance: A legal late action can fool a committed swing but cannot create an unreadable unavoidable strike for a waiting hitter.
decisions.accepted_scope: Retain live left/right steering after release, with bounded, readable break that gives the hitter a fair opportunity to respond. Do not select a release-locked trajectory or an early-steering-only lockout. Exact break strength, response timing, per-pitch/charge differences and numerical limits remain open. This is direction acceptance only, with no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-04: 1. Keep live left/right steering with limits that give the hitter a readable chance to respond; 2. Lock the path at release; 3. Allow steering early, then lock it.

history.author: Jack
history.scope: Retain live left/right steering after release, with bounded, readable break that gives the hitter a fair opportunity to respond. Do not select a release-locked trajectory or an early-steering-only lockout. Exact break strength, response timing, per-pitch/charge differences and numerical limits remain open. decisions.question: What makes a pitch well executed?

options.label: Existing charge/release
options.tradeoff: Preserve a simple timing commitment with visible benefits and fatigue costs.

options.label: Power versus command
options.tradeoff: Use the same action to trade strength against controllability; adds a tactical risk.

options.label: Separate accuracy task
options.tradeoff: Meter, pulse or gesture execution; greater precision cost every pitch.

decisions.recommendation: A initially; consider B if it creates a clear choice. Avoid a second execution minigame unless PH-01 selects that emphasis.
decisions.existing_contract: No charge timing, Nice multiplier or stamina number changes with this direction.
decisions.acceptance: A player can distinguish a poor release from a poor location choice; maximum power is not universally best.
decisions.accepted_scope: Add a stronger power-versus-control tradeoff within the same charge/release controls: pursuing more pitch power makes the pitch harder to control. The form of the control challenge, affected pitches, exact charge/release behavior, fatigue interaction and numerical values remain open. This does not select a separate accuracy minigame or a particular random-error model. Preserve PH-03 mound/shape location and PH-04 live steering. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decisions.recommendation: A for the ordinary duel; C is useful in training. Choose any competitive assistance openly in PH-17.
decisions.existing_contract: One shared screen and both controller seats must be considered. No new overlay is approved.
decisions.acceptance: Two people on one screen retain a mind game; a learner can identify the cue that gave them a chance to respond.

decisions.question: What reaction and between-pitch pace should we target?

options.label: Keep current pace
options.tradeoff: Re-sit existing timing before changing the budget.

options.label: Faster duel
options.tradeoff: Increase urgency after measured evidence; raises accessibility demands.

options.label: Selected middle ground
options.tradeoff: Tune pitch families and reset rhythm to an explicit measured budget.

decisions.recommendation: A until the gameplay-spec D7 re-sit; then compare matched captures and authored trial intervals.
decisions.existing_contract: D7 is a HOLD, not superseded by this brief. Air time, visual tell time, input lead and reset duration are separate clocks.
decisions.acceptance: Record release, readable cue, swing command and plate arrival; Jack compares pad, keyboard and two-pad play before numeric acceptance.
decisions.accepted_scope: Keep the current pace until Jack replays it, with a preference for slightly slower overall rhythm if needed to let character animations, highlights, side changes and special-ability clips read. Do not pursue a faster duel by default. This qualifies option A with modest presentation breathing room, not a blanket slowdown or a selected pitch-flight change. Evaluate ball travel/reaction time separately from animation and transition durations. Preserve the D7 named standalone re-sit before numeric pitch-speed tuning; no timing values, clip cadence, camera treatment or final playtest acceptance are selected. Coordinate the existing F693-07 deliberate dead-ball pacing direction and presentation owners; keep live baseball judgment in Sim. Direction acceptance only; no runtime, presentation or art change.

decision_evidence.question: PH-07: What pace should we pursue? 1. Keep current pace until you replay it (recommended): use that session to decide whether reaction time or between-pitch rhythm needs changing. 2. Presented option 1 maps to canonical A, qualified by Jack’s preference for slightly slower pacing to highlight animations and game moments.

decisions.question: What should fatigue change during a short game?

options.label: Current pitch-use resource
options.tradeoff: Keep per-character fatigue and swaps; audit costs and tells.

options.label: Visible effort economy
options.tradeoff: Make high-effort choices the main cost, with gradual readable degradation.

options.label: Minimal fatigue influence
options.tradeoff: Keep the duel stable; removes some substitution and resource strategy.

decisions.recommendation: Compare A/B after the pitch vocabulary is chosen; no invisible sudden loss of control.
decisions.existing_contract: Existing stamina costs stack; a changeup adds 3 to the ordinary cost of 4. No new fatigue thresholds selected.
decisions.acceptance: The player predicts when to change pitchers and understands why a tired delivery differs; swapping does not erase history.
decisions.accepted_scope: Use gradual, clearly visible, effort-driven pitcher fatigue. Ordinary pitching is relatively economical; repeatedly pushing for power wears the pitcher down faster. Effectiveness declines gradually rather than through an unexplained sudden loss of control. Exact stamina pools, action costs, fatigue curve, affected abilities, recovery/substitution details and numeric penalties remain open. Coordinate accumulated fatigue with PH-05’s immediate power/control tradeoff and PH-15’s character differences, without assuming a particular stacking formula. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-08: 1. Keep current pitch-use stamina and tired/exhausted thresholds; 2. Gradual, effort-driven fatigue: economical ordinary pitching, more wear from repeatedly pushing power, gradual visible decline; 3. Keep fatigue minor.

options.tradeoff: Add a coarse high/low adjustment; more coverage decisions without a free cursor.

options.label: Independent two-dimensional cursor

decisions.question: How should timing and barrel position determine contact quality?

options.label: Preserve the existing split
options.tradeoff: Position primarily controls quality; timing controls direction/whiffs, with the current rim exception audited.

options.label: Continuous combined quality
options.tradeoff: Timing and spatial error both reduce quality; expressive but may punish one mistake twice.

options.label: Timing-led assistance
options.tradeoff: Timing drives the accessible mode with explicit spatial assistance; less direct coverage control.

decisions.recommendation: A as the baseline. Make the current timing-rim quality demotion explicit before deciding to retain or replace it.
decisions.existing_contract: Gameplay-spec D4/D13 govern. Code demotes one tier at the outer timing rim; do not claim timing never affects quality today.
decisions.acceptance: Controlled early/late and centered/off-center trials explain quality and direction without guaranteed hits or arbitrary outs.
decisions.accepted_scope: Keep placement as the primary determinant of contact quality and timing as the determinant of pull/opposite-field direction within the contact window. Centered contact can remain strong when deliberately early or late, with weaker contact near the timing-window edges and a miss outside the window. Retain the timing-rim penalty concept rather than continuously reducing quality with every departure from ideal timing. Exact window widths, edge bands and penalty amounts remain unselected; existing gameplay-spec D4/D13 govern until explicitly amended. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-10: 1. Placement primarily controls quality; timing controls direction, weakens contact near the window edges and misses outside it; 2. Placement and timing both continuously control quality.

decisions.question: What is the tradeoff between a quick swing and charging?

options.label: One hold/release grammar
options.tradeoff: Keep quick and charged versions of one action, including overcharge.

options.label: Explicit contact/power choices
options.tradeoff: Separate intent selection; easier intent clarity but more inputs.

options.label: Minimal charging
options.tradeoff: Emphasize timing/coverage with little load management; changes the Mario rhythm.

decisions.recommendation: A, provided quick swings retain useful situational advantages. Compare forgiveness, power and commitment as a package.
decisions.existing_contract: Existing fill/MAX/decay values are a snapshot, not approved new targets; preserve D13 until explicitly amended.
decisions.acceptance: Quick swings remain useful with two strikes and awkward pitches; waiting fully charged is not a dominant strategy.
decisions.accepted_scope: Keep quick and charged swings on one button using the same hold/release action. Quick release favors contact; holding and releasing favors power with more commitment, and holding too long loses charge. Quick swings must remain useful for two-strike protection and difficult pitches rather than being dominated by charging. Exact fill time, MAX hold, decay, forgiveness, power and commitment values remain open. Preserve the PH-09 cursor and PH-10 contact-quality direction, and existing D13 until explicitly amended. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-11: 1. One button, quick or charged: quick release favors contact, holding/releasing favors power with more commitment, holding too long loses charge; 2. Separate contact and power choices; 3. Reduce charging substantially. Quick swings should remain useful for two strikes and difficult pitches.

decisions.question: How deliberately can the hitter shape a batted ball?

options.label: Current bounded influence
options.tradeoff: Timing pulls/pushes; stick shifts direction and loft, with contact constraining the result.

options.label: Preselected approach
options.tradeoff: Choose grounder/liner/lift intent before commitment; more tactical clarity.

options.label: Contact geometry alone
options.tradeoff: Remove extra trajectory intent; simpler inputs but fewer deliberate situational choices.

decisions.recommendation: A first; retain meaningful influence without letting a stick command guarantee a hit class.
decisions.existing_contract: Current Up lowers launch and Down lifts. Coordinate changed exit/launch distributions with #693/#708/#715.
decisions.acceptance: The same intent can succeed or fail because of actual contact; grounders, liners, flies and fouls remain distinct.
decisions.accepted_scope: Remove extra directional input for shaping ordinary hits. Timing, contact position, pitch shape and swing type determine batted-ball flight; retain PH-09 horizontal batter positioning, PH-10 timing-led pull/opposite-field direction and contact-quality rules, and PH-11 quick/charged swings. Do not add a preselected grounder/liner/lift approach. This selects a target departure from gameplay-spec sections 5.3–5.4 direct stick spray/loft influence, to reconcile before implementation. It does not remove batter movement or SET recenter, change pitching steering, settle bunt placement, require mesh-collision microphysics, or select flight coefficients. Direction only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-12: 1. Influence direction and loft with the stick; 2. Choose a grounder/liner/lift approach beforehand; 3. No extra directional input: timing, contact position, pitch shape and swing type determine flight.

decisions.question: What happens when the hitter changes their mind?

options.label: Existing commitment
options.tradeoff: Keep taking and committed swings; make release semantics clear.

options.label: Deterministic check/cancel
options.tradeoff: Add a taught cancel boundary before commitment; more plate discipline control.

options.label: Assisted checking
options.tradeoff: Infer hesitation and rescue some swings; easier but risks surprising judgments.

decisions.recommendation: A initially; B only if Jack wants checking as a core verb. Avoid hidden random check-swing outcomes.
decisions.existing_contract: A release-based charge scheme needs an explicit distinction between canceling a load and swinging. No new binding selected.
decisions.acceptance: Take, load-cancel, bunt withdrawal and swing cannot conflict; balls/strikes follow the same geometric zone.
decisions.accepted_scope: Add a deliberate player-commanded cancel before swing commitment, allowing the hitter to abandon a charged swing and take the pitch. Once the swing is committed, it follows through. Keep cancel distinct from the existing release-to-swing action. The cancel input, exact commitment/cutoff boundary, input priority and subsequent rearming behavior remain open. This selects neither automatic hesitation detection nor a mid-swing rescue. Preserve PH-09–PH-12 and existing geometric ball/strike judgment. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

decision_evidence.question: PH-13: 1. Keep release-to-commit with no separate cancel; 2. Add a deliberate cancel before commitment: abandon a charged swing and take the pitch, with committed swings following through; 3. Assisted checking that interprets hesitation.

history.author: Jack
history.scope: Add a deliberate player-commanded cancel before swing commitment, allowing the hitter to abandon a charged swing and take the pitch. Once the swing is committed, it follows through. Keep cancel distinct from the existing release-to-swing action. The cancel input, exact commitment/cutoff boundary, input priority and subsequent rearming behavior remain open. This selects neither automatic hesitation detection nor a mid-swing rescue. Preserve PH-09–PH-12 and existing geometric ball/strike judgment. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.

validation_requirements: A deliberate cancel before commitment takes the pitch and does not accidentally produce a swing when the canceled load button is released.
A cancel after commitment does not undo the swing, contact or its judgment.

decisions.question: How much depth belongs in bunting?

options.label: Simple situational bunt
options.tradeoff: Preserve existing square/contact behavior and teach placement and foul risk.

options.label: Richer bunt control
options.tradeoff: Add placement or timing demands for sacrifice/drag intent; increases state and input work.

options.label: Defer expansion
options.tradeoff: Keep the current verb while first settling ordinary swings.

decisions.recommendation: A/C during initial design, then test B only against a concrete situational need.
decisions.existing_contract: Existing S-18/19 and two-strike foul-bunt rules remain; do not create a guaranteed CPU exploit.

discussion.user_question: Bunt quality should be determined by contact quality?
discussion.recommendation: Yes: use actual contact quality, interpreted through a bunt-specific response. Good contact should deaden and control the ball; poor contact can produce an uncontrolled pop, excessive pace or a foul according to contact/pitch geometry. Preserve legal contact and take/miss judgment; no separate bunt-quality meter or random safe/out result. Good bunting should not inherit the ordinary swing meaning of better contact equals greater exit speed.
discussion.baseline_evidence: At baseline 05471a6, AtBatResolver.cs:58–64 determines contact quality; :107–114 applies the bunt exit multiplier and pops sour contact or high pitches. Exit speed first inherits swing quality/power factors at :81–89. Contact quality already matters, but this does not establish a dedicated deadening/control quality curve.
